reason: The passage is explicitly religious and cosmic in nature, not political. It depicts God's miraculous intervention on behalf of the Hebrews—the burning bush vision, divine signs (staff to serpent, leprous hand healed, water to blood), and God's direct promise to deliver them from Egyptian bondage. The motivation is God's compassion for their suffering (רָאֹה רָאִיתִי אֶת־ עֳנִי עַמִּי—'I have surely seen the affliction of my people'), and the mission is explicitly religious: to sacrifice to the Lord (וְנִזְבְּחָה לַֽיהוָה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ). The people's belief is rooted in God's divine visitation and miraculous signs, not political organizing. There is no portrayal of political struggle, rebellion, or liberty-fighting—only the cosmic drama of God's miraculous deliverance.
